newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah volatile on band rumours.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah volatile on band rumours.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was volatile against the dollar in active late trading on Friday following renewed rumours that the central bank's intervention band would be widened, dealers said.
They said offshore operators, mostly in Singapore, started the band speculation with dollar selling as the central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono delivered a speech in Hong Kong.
"We don't know what the speech was about. But immediately after the governor started his speech, the dollar was down."
Djiwandono however made no reference to the band during his speech.

Spot rupiah rose to 2,394.00/94.25 from 2,395.5/96.0 on the rumours before settling at 2,394.0/94.8 at 0915 GMT. It opened at 2,394.25/95.00. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,394.0/94.5 and 2,395.2/95.5, respectively.
The rupiah weakened in the morning on excess supply.

One local bank dealer said it was also possible that the dollar's decline in the afternoon could be linked to a brief tightening in the money market. Overnight rupiah rose briefly to a high of 11.0 percent from six percent before settling at 5.0/7.0 percent.
The dealer said a sudden rise in overnight money might have made operators nervous and triggered some dollar selling.
"But surprisingly when rupiah liquidity turns ample, the market appears to be bearish on dollars," one U.S. bank dealer said, adding that swaps were also higher.
Overnight swap was at 0.1/0.2 and tom/next at 0.15/0.25.
One-month swaps were at 11.0/12.0, two at 24.5/26.0, three at 37.5/38.5 and six at 77.5/78.5 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,385/2,577 and the conversion band at 2,385/2,433 on Friday.
